subject: Food Science
title: Listeria
description: A fast breakdown of Listeria for builders.

hook.text: Listeria kills 20–30% of people it infects seriously. It's one of the deadliest foodborne pathogens.

buildup.text: Listeria monocytogenes grows at fridge temperatures, in high-salt conditions, and in vacuum-packed foods.

discovery.text: It targets pregnant women, newborns, the elderly, and the immunocompromised. It can cross the placental barrier.

twist.text: Unlike most bacteria, Listeria doesn't make food smell or look spoiled. The food seems perfectly normal.

climax.text: Deli meats, soft cheeses, and smoked fish are the highest-risk foods. The 2011 cantaloupe outbreak killed 33 people.

punchline.text: No smell, no sign—just deadly. Listeria is the silent killer in your fridge.

quiz.question: What makes Listeria especially dangerous?
options: It grows at fridge temperatures and doesn't change food's smell or appearance
